steps.notes: PASS, but ONLY with one specific Metropolis variant (random site via randint, num_steps*N attempts, rand drawn only on uphill moves); 7 other standard variants fail all 3 tests.
Deterministic; pairwise i<j overlaps sorted ascending; target length 10=C(5,2) confirms the convention. Clean.
PASS with std-threshold 1.4/sqrt(N); but the cutoff is unstated and tests 0/1 use UNSEEDED np.random.normal inputs.
PASS only with J=(randn+randn.T)/2/sqrt(N) (contradicts background's 'n_ij iid N(0,1)') AND batch replica initialization. Documented J recipe fails. Joint run ~4 min (within official 1800 s).

findings.evidence: Targets are EXACT frozen spin configurations from a Metropolis trajectory, so the solver's RNG-consumption pattern is the de-facto spec (pattern 14.1, 'hidden seeds & statistical asserts'). Variant scan (review/work/50/scan_step1.py) over 8 standard implementations: site selection {randint-per-attempt, sequential sweep} x attempt count {num_steps*N, num_steps} x acceptance {rand only when dE>0, rand every attempt}. ONLY ('rand','perspin','cond') matches all 3 targets; all others fail all 3. In particular the equally-textbook acceptance form `if np.random.rand() < np.exp(-dE/T): flip` (rand drawn unconditionally; correct Metropolis, identical equilibrium distribution) fails every test because it consumes the RNG stream differently. The prompt's hints ('number of sampling steps per spin', 'only randint and rand are allowed') pin the site selection and attempt count, but nothing states that rand must be drawn only for uphill moves (dE<=0 auto-accepted). A competent solver faces a coin flip between two equally-correct acceptance implementations; the losing one scores 0.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) specify the update loop exactly in the docstring (pseudocode: per attempt draw i=np.random.randint(N); compute dE=2*spins[i]*J[i]@spins; flip if dE<=0, else flip iff np.random.rand()<exp(-dE/T); repeat num_steps*N times), or (b) replace exact-configuration asserts with statistical checks (final energy within a band, |magnetization| bound) that any correct Metropolis sampler satisfies.

findings.evidence: The judging criterion is left to the solver: prompt says only 'A broader distribution or multi-modal behavior indicates potential replica symmetry breaking ... allow some reasonable deviation in the judging criterion.' Targets are (False, True, True) where test 1 feeds N(0, sqrt(3)/sqrt(N)) - i.e. std exactly 1.73x the replica-symmetric 1/sqrt(N), deliberately in the gray zone. Threshold scan (review/work/50/scan_step3.py, 200 random draws of the unseeded inputs): criteria 'std > f/sqrt(N)' pass with probability 1.0 only for f in [1.1, 1.6]; f=1.7 passes 80%, f=1.73 passes 51%, f=1.8 passes 2.5%, f=2.0 passes 0%. A solver reading 'reasonable deviation' as 'within a factor of 2' fails deterministically. Step 50.4's test 0 further narrows the safe band: its overlap std is 1.147/sqrt(N) and must classify as False, so thresholds below ~1.15 fail there. The intended cutoff (somewhere in (1.15,1.6)) is stated nowhere. (Side note: tests never penalize ignoring N - an absolute threshold std>0.15 also passes all 50.3 and 50.4 tests.)
findings.suggested_fix: State the criterion in the docstring, e.g. 'return True iff the sample standard deviation of overlaps exceeds 1.5/sqrt(N)', and regenerate targets if needed.

findings.evidence: Tests 0 and 1 generate their inputs with UNSEEDED RNG: 'overlaps = np.random.normal(0, 1/np.sqrt(N), size=1000)' (no np.random.seed anywhere in this step's test cases). Every scoring run therefore evaluates the solver's function on different data. For criteria near the decision boundary the official verdict is flaky run-to-run (measured: threshold 1.7/sqrt(N) -> 80% pass rate; 1.73 -> 51%). The boolean target is fixed but the input is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add np.random.seed(<k>) at the top of each test case (as steps 50.1 and 50.4 already do).

findings.evidence: Background states: 'J_ij \equiv n_ij/\sqrt{N}, and n_ij's are i.i.d. from N(0,1)' - i.e. coupling variance 1/N. The frozen targets are reproducible ONLY with J = (A + A.T)/2 / sqrt(N), A = np.random.randn(N,N), np.fill_diagonal(J,0) - i.e. coupling variance 1/(2N), HALF the documented value (and a different RNG trace). Verified by variant scan (review/work/50/scan_step4.py): the averaged-symmetrization recipe matches target test 0 bit-exactly (mean +0.0005191837, std 0.1147205648); the literal i.i.d.-N(0,1) recipe (upper triangle mirrored) gives mean -0.0009485714, std 0.1276461236 - fails. The official prompt template (SciCode/eval/data/background_comment_template.txt) never shows test cases, so the (J+J.T)/2 recipe visible in 50.1's test code is NOT available to the solver; the background's formula is the only J spec, and following it guarantees failure. The exact-match float assert (np.allclose on mean/std of a ~6e7-call RNG trace) leaves zero slack.
findings.suggested_fix: Either change the background to 'generate A=np.random.randn(N,N), set J=(A+A.T)/2, zero the diagonal, divide by sqrt(N)' (matching the target), or regenerate targets with the documented i.i.d. variance-1/N couplings. Also consider asserting statistical properties (|mean|<tol, std within a band) instead of exact floats.

findings.evidence: Beyond the J recipe (separate D10 finding), the exact float targets force two more unstated RNG-ordering guesses. (1) Replica initialization order: the spec ('For each J, create many replicas of the system by randomly choose sigma_i in {+-1} as the starting state and find the equilibrium states') is satisfied both by interleaved (init replica k, equilibrate it, repeat) and batch (draw ALL num_replicas initial states, then equilibrate each) loops; only BATCH matches the target (interleaved: mean +0.0001224490 vs target +0.0005191837). (2) The solver's find_equilibrium from step 50.1 must itself be the unique trace-matching variant - a solver whose 50.1 already failed for RNG-trace reasons automatically fails 50.4 too. Compounded, a competent solver must win at least three independent unstated-implementation coin flips for the floats to match.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the loop structure (draw all initial replica states before equilibrating, reuse step-1's update rule verbatim) or switch the assert to tolerance-banded statistics rather than exact RNG-trace floats.

overall_assessment: Steps 50.2 and 50.3-as-implemented are fine mechanically, but this problem is dominated by frozen exact-match targets sitting on top of a stochastic simulation: the targets encode one specific RNG-consumption trace, so equally-correct Metropolis implementations (unconditional accept-rand, interleaved replica init) score 0, and 50.4's target additionally encodes a J-coupling variance that contradicts its own background text (1/(2N) vs documented 1/N) with no way for the solver to discover this since test cases are hidden. Step 50.3's pass band for the unstated RSB cutoff is roughly (1.15, 1.6)/sqrt(N) and its tests use unseeded inputs. As-is, a competent solver's expected score on 50.1/50.4 is closer to a multi-way coin flip than a measure of skill; 50.4 in particular is unfair to score as written.
